sentences.sentence: NHS inform lists asthma attacks, pneumonia and heart failure among the likely causes of sudden breathlessness.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages). | second pass: supported

sentences.sentence: NHS inform also lists a severe allergic reaction, a collapsed lung and a blood clot in the lung as possible causes of sudden breathlessness.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: NHS inform lists allergic reaction, pneumothorax and pulmonary embolism, but retrieved text does not call them 'less common'.

sentences.sentence: A collapsed lung, or pneumothorax, is a partial collapse of the lung caused by a small tear in the lung surface.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: NHS inform text: pneumothorax is partial collapse of the lung caused by a small tear in the lung surface. No retrieved text defined pulmonary embolism as a blockage in a lung blood vessel (only 'blood clot in the lung'). Attribution to nhs.uk not shown.

sentences.sentence: The NHS lists several possible causes of breathlessness, including COPD, scarring of the lungs, heart failure, asthma, chest infections and being overweight.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Retrieved NHS text lists COPD, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, heart failure, lung cancer, asthma, chest infection, being overweight and smoking. Being unfit, anaemia and heart rhythm problems were not retrieved; 'commonly' not supported.

sentences.sentence: In heart failure, fluid builds up in the lungs and makes breathing harder.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages). | second pass: supported

sentences.sentence: Sudden breathlessness could be an asthma attack, which makes it difficult to move air in and out of the airways.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: NHS inform: sudden breathlessness could be an asthma attack, difficult to move air in and out of airways. Narrowing, sticky mucus, wheeze and cough not found in retrieved text.

sentences.sentence: The NHS lists breathlessness as the most common symptom of heart failure; it may happen after activity or at rest, may be worse when lying down, and may wake a person at night.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages). | second pass: supported

sentences.sentence: It lists tiredness, swollen ankles and legs, and feeling lightheaded or fainting as other heart failure symptoms.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages). | second pass: supported

sentences.sentence: An NHS trust leaflet says the most common symptom of a pulmonary embolism is breathlessness, with chest pain that is worse on breathing or coughing, and it also lists cough and fever.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: North Tees leaflet: breathlessness most common; chest pain worse on breathing or coughing; fever alongside cough. Coughing up blood came from a different trust leaflet (Royal Berkshire), not confirmed for this one.

sentences.sentence: NHS inform says to call 999 or go to A&E for severe difficulty breathing, such as being unable to speak without pausing for breath.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages). | second pass: supported

sentences.sentence: The NHS says chest tightness or heaviness, or pain that spreads to the arms, back, neck or jaw, is also a reason to call 999 or go to A&E.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Chest tightness / pain to arms, back, neck, jaw as 999 reasons were found on the NHS (England) page and NHS 111 Wales, not confirmed on NHS inform. Wrong publisher.

sentences.sentence: The NHS adds sudden confusion, or lips or skin turning pale, blue or grey, to the signs for calling 999 or going to A&E.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Sudden confusion and pale, blue or grey lips or skin as 999/A&E signs are on the NHS shortness of breath page and NHS 111 Wales; Conwy practice page not returned, so attribution to a GP practice page is unverified.

sentences.sentence: NHS 111 Wales advises that a person should not drive themselves to A&E but should ask someone to take them or call an ambulance.
sentences.note: Returned search text for this page said this (summary blends pages). | second pass: supported

sentences.sentence: The NHS says to contact NHS 111 for difficulty breathing, feeling or being sick, coughing up blood, or pain or swelling in one leg.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Retrieved NHS text sends these symptoms (difficulty breathing, feeling or being sick, coughing up blood, pain or swelling in one leg) to NHS 111; 'or the GP' and 'worsening breathlessness' were not in that list. Changes route to care.

sentences.sentence: NHS inform advises contacting the GP practice if breathlessness is new or unexplained.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: NHS inform: contact GP practice if breathlessness is new or unexplained. 'Urgently' and the 'airways or heart' reasoning not found for sudden breathlessness.

sentences.sentence: The NHS advises seeing a GP if breathlessness has lasted longer than a month, gets worse with normal activity or when lying down, or comes with swollen ankles.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Summary of NHS page: see a GP if breathlessness lasts longer than a month, worsens with activity or lying down, or comes with swollen ankles. Attributed to NHS inform in the draft, but found on the NHS page.

sentences.sentence: NHS inform's guidance asks whether breathlessness came on suddenly or slowly and whether anything triggered it, such as exercise.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Not found as a GP-questions list. NHS inform asks whether it came on suddenly or slowly and whether anything triggered it such as exercise.

sentences.sentence: An NHS England pathway for persistent breathlessness lists an ECG, a chest X-ray and spirometry among the first-line tests.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: NHS England tool (chronic breathlessness, over 8 weeks) lists ECG, chest X-ray and spirometry as first-line; blood tests not confirmed for this tool (NT-proBNP was in a different regional pathway).

sentences.sentence: Spirometry is a breathing test that measures how much air a person can blow out and how fast.
sentences.note: Plain textbook definition. | second pass: textbook

sentences.sentence: The same pathway says an ECG showing atrial fibrillation with breathlessness should prompt a heart specialist assessment, including an echocardiogram.
sentences.note: Edited after second pass: Retrieved text: ECG showing atrial fibrillation prompts cardiology assessment including echocardiography; further investigation planned at a multidisciplinary meeting. CT scan and ambulatory ECG monitoring not confirmed.

sentences.sentence: Treatment depends on the cause.

sentences.sentence: For COPD, treatment usually involves relieving symptoms with medicines such as inhalers, and pulmonary rehabilitation may help.

sentences.sentence: Heart failure is managed with lifestyle changes and medicines or surgery.

sentences.sentence: A blood clot in the lung can be treated with anticoagulants, which are drugs that thin the blood.

sentences.sentence: NHS leaflets describe pursed-lip breathing as a technique that can help keep the airways open for longer and reduce the work of breathing, for example in COPD.
